top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz) recognises one identifiable discovery: productivity differences across firms drive selection into exporting and foreign investment, so trade reallocates activity across firms and adds a channel to the gains from trade. Melitz (2003) is the canonical selection model, and Helpman, Melitz and Yeaple (2004) add the exports-versus-FDI sorting result. The core is more than twenty years old, has been tested repeatedly in firm-level data, and was extended where the baseline failed in detail. The main residual risk is attribution, since Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are not credited. I judge that manageable with a narrow citation limited to selection and reallocation that makes no claim about welfare magnitudes, with the empirical precursors acknowledged in the scientific background. The case would weaken if the Committee defined the discovery as the whole firm-level and quantitative trade programme. P001 is clearly preferable to no award because the achievement is mature and its credit boundary is defensible. The unanimous support in round 2 is not evidence of merit, because the files share one model and reasoning patterns.
recusal_note: No connection to Helpman or Melitz is apparent from the profile. Disclosed without adjudication: my research on exchange-rate pass-through, invoicing currency and pricing under imperfect competition is adjacent to trade and industrial organisation. I co-authored a menu-cost paper (IJIO 2026) with chair John Hassler and Tore Ellingsen. My spouse, Magdalena Andersson, is a public fact noted only for disclosure, and no bearing on the candidates is apparent.
